skills.content:
Start with rho_index: select an owner or search, then rho_resolve only the operations
needed now. Use rho_call with the complete contractRef. The private connection supplies
the project; discovery never grants additional authority or starts a runtime.
Large replies carry a result reference. Use rho_read to inspect its fields and fetch
only selected text ranges or array pages. Retain useful references; release finished
results explicitly. Never repeat an action just to retrieve a large reply.
Writes use their owner’s conditions and original identity. A lost acknowledgement
requires observing that request; unchanged work never receives a replacement ID.
Declare produced figures as media. resource.list or artifact.check returns their
registered references; bind those directly with composition.apply, including artifacts
inside owner state. Do not manually register internal paths. A layout acknowledgement
alone does not prove the browser displayed the result.
People and Agents share the document buffer and conditional save operation.

failureRecipes.next: Call protocol.validate on the same body and apply the named fix.

failureRecipes.message: Version or revision changed.
failureRecipes.next: Re-read the owner record and retry with its current numbers, keeping your original changeId for the same request only.

failureRecipes.message: Observation missed events.
failureRecipes.next: Read a fresh snapshot; do not replay acknowledged writes.

skills.content:
A person opens a folder themselves; an Agent is not required to read it.

1. project.entries lists one level of a folder inside the project, bounded and
   confined to the project root, skipping owner state and symbolic links. Pass path
   to descend; ".." and absolute paths are refused.
2. project.openFile opens one text file as a document and places a single editor
   view for it in the tab layout. Opening the same file again folds into one view.
3. A file the person opened is a document in the shared buffer: they and the Agent
   edit and conditionally save the same text.

The boundary is deliberate and worth stating to a person who asks: a tab may read
its folder, edit a buffer and conditionally save it; it may not register resources, run
anything or reach a sibling project. Those stay Agent or operator work. When a
person expects otherwise, say which rule refuses them rather than reporting a bug.

Files the project shows as registered are not the same as files in the folder: the
sidebar counts registered resources, while the Overview lists the folder itself.
skills.intent: Let a person read and open files from the folder they selected, without an Agent.

failureRecipes.next: A source folder added to the project is listed through the project, not by absolute path.

skills.content:
Describe the whole task yourself: Rho fixes no closed list of kinds or states.

1. task.map.declare carries stable item IDs, your own kind and state words (each a
   label, an optional tone and an optional role Rho understands: working, waiting,
   done, planned, unknown, stopped), titles you write, progress counted from real
   receipts, an optional layout view per item, and next only for steps you will take.
2. task.map.present changes a card form, its parameters (a subset), or the focus.
   People use the same call. A pinned target, or a change within agentFormIntervalMs
   of your last applied form change, is merged into one pending suggestion instead of
   being applied: the screen stays steady and the person applies it.
3. task.map.respond is the person only: pin, unpin, revert your form change (layout
   only, never the work), accept or dismiss a suggestion.
4. task.map.read observes. Reading never starts, resumes or reruns work.

A form declared zoom: false is reached only by naming it, so stepping up from a card
lands on the summary, not on compare.

skills.content:
Edit a document buffer with a stable identity, explicit undo and conditional saves.
Use capability.list to discover the document operations this session may call.

1. document.open takes a project-relative path and returns the buffer with id, version
   and revision. Inside the project, never under .rho or .git: internal state is not
   an editable document.
2. Writes are conditional. document.edit takes expectedVersion and, when changeId is
   given, expectedRevision as well: the two travel together, always. A refused edit
   leaves the buffer and undo untouched; re-read and retry with the current numbers
   rather than replaying the old request under a new identity.
3. Undo has three distinct meanings. document.undoOwn reverses only the caller's own
   latest complete retained input group. document.revert reverses one named active
   change, possibly by another author, through targetChangeId. document.undo is the
   legacy global form and is not the human keyboard shortcut.
4. document.save writes disk only when the expected disk digest still matches. After
   a lost reply the save is pending: read the buffer to see pendingSave, and either
   resume the same request or abandon it with document.abandonSave, which never
   writes disk and keeps the buffer.
5. History is author-scoped. document.history lists retained entries;
   document.change.read returns exact before and after text for one change.

A browser tab may read and edit but never save: saving is an Agent or operator step.
Live editor bindings use {kind:"live-document",documentId}; a pinned binding keeps an
exact version and stays exact.
skills.intent: Edit a document buffer conditionally, with explicit undo and save conditions.

skills.content:
Keep resource identity and provenance explicit: bytes, a version, and where they came from.
Use capability.list to discover resource.list, resource.read, resource.register and artifact.check.

1. resource.register declares existing bytes with their kind and format, and requires
   expectedDigest of the current content. The returned {id, version} names those exact
   bytes; when the file changes, both change and old pages become stale on purpose.
2. resource.read is a bounded byte read with offset; resource.list reports retained
   resources with availability. Reads never start a runtime and never execute R.
3. artifact.check verifies the artifacts one run declared, against the completion
   inventory the producer wrote. Without a declared inventory there is nothing to
   check, and a missing inventory is not evidence of a missing artifact.
4. resource.list and artifact.check return registered references for declared run
   artifacts, including owner-state files. Bind those references directly to a view;
   resource.register remains limited to ordinary project files.

Declare a table key and namespace at registration if a later comparison or plot needs
entity identity; an unkeyed table stays readable but has no identity to compare on.
skills.intent: Register existing bytes with explicit identity, read them bounded, and verify produced artifacts.

skills.content:
Run R in this project. Use capability.list to discover object.read, action.submit and
artifact.check in this session; reads address exported snapshots and execution is one
explicit submit that keeps its original operation identity.

1. Find the script. A disk script must match its declared digest; a buffer script is
   pinned by documentId and version. The bytes sent are the bytes in this request.
   If a body is not certain, protocol.validate { method, body } answers with the edit
   each problem needs before anything is sent.
2. Declare what the run produces, not what it might produce: artifacts carry path,
   kind and format, and their paths stay inside the run output directory.
3. The output directory exists before R starts and is handed to R as its first
   argument (commandArgs(trailingOnly = TRUE)[1]). Write there directly; do not build
   the directory and do not use the working directory for outputs.
4. If you need artifact verification, declare completion: its filename is relative to
   the run directory, beside artifacts/, and the producer writes
   {"schemaVersion":1,"complete":true,"artifacts":[{"path","bytes","sha256"}]}.
   artifact.check reads that inventory; without it there is nothing to verify.
5. Read the outcome. A read of the operation reports the current outcome, so no
   separate observe is required: action.lookup and action.list reconcile a run that
   finished while nobody was watching. When the Host gives no answer the run stays
   active and the outcome is genuinely unknown; do not resubmit under a new identity.
6. Facts belong to the session that submitted the run. Another session looking up the
   same operationId gets not found, so check artifacts from the submitting session.

An executed artifact lives under owner state (.rho/plugins/runs/...). It is verified
through artifact.check; it is not a project resource, so resource.register refuses it
and an Agent-run figure cannot be shown in a view. Do not claim it is presented.

skills.content:
Check that the packages an R script needs are usable, and prepare them explicitly.
Use capability.list to discover requirements.check and requirements.prepare.

1. requirements.check probes the declared packages with bounded base R and reports what
   is present, absent or unknown. It installs nothing and starts no Host.
2. requirements.prepare returns an explicit native plan: the code, arguments and the
   library path it would use. It is a plan, not permission, and it never installs
   packages silently.
3. Base R needs no declaration. Declare only add-on packages, each with its source, and
   keep the declaration with the original request identity.
4. The project library path is fixed per project; a check that reports a package present
   is still not a promise that the run will succeed.

skills.content:
Read and compare typed tables through stable resource identities.
Use capability.list to discover data.page, data.compare and resource.register.

1. Register the bytes first with resource.register and keep the returned {id, version}.
   A version names exact bytes: if the file changed, the version changes and the old
   pages become stale rather than silently mixing.
2. data.page takes offset and limit, an optional sort and an optional filter. It never
   addresses rows by position as identity: identity is the declared entity key, and an
   unkeyed table is readable but has none, so do not fabricate one.
3. data.compare joins two keyed tables and returns a new resource with provenance.
   The join is left, inner or full on declared key columns and namespaces.
4. Nulls stay nulls. A declared null value is not an empty string, and a comparison
   that finds no value on one side reports no value, not "absent from the file".

Reads are bounded observations: they never execute R and never change a resource.
skills.intent: Page and compare a typed table without inventing identity from row order.

failureRecipes.message: Resource version changed.

failureRecipes.message: Page size exceeds the configured limit.
failureRecipes.next: Ask for fewer rows; the earlier rows stay readable.

failureRecipes.message: Filter or sort names an unknown column.
failureRecipes.next: Use a declared column name from the registration, not a positional index.

failureRecipes.message: Compare needs two keyed tables in declared namespaces.
failureRecipes.next: Declare a key column and namespace at registration before comparing.

verify.description: Declared types keep leading zeros and literal NA, joins retain nulls, namespaces and both input versions, and unkeyed tables never fabricate keys.

presentation.description: Teaches Claude Code to use declared types, stable keys and exact table versions.

skills.content:
Describe and select a region of registered media without touching its bytes.
Use capability.list to discover media.describe and object.read.

1. Register the media first and keep its exact {id, version}. Coordinates are declared
   in original media space: width and height come from the declaration, not from what a
   renderer happens to show.
2. media.describe reports the stored description of that version. Rendering is optional
   and never changes source bytes; a region selection maps back to original coordinates.
3. A region outside the declared bounds is refused rather than clamped, so a zoomed or
   cropped view cannot invent pixels that are not in the file.
4. If the file changed, the version is stale: register the new bytes instead of reusing
   coordinates that belonged to the old ones.
skills.intent: Describe media and select a region in original coordinates.

failureRecipes.message: Region lies outside the declared media bounds.
failureRecipes.next: Use coordinates inside width and height from the registration; a region is never clamped.

failureRecipes.message: Resource version changed.
failureRecipes.next: Re-register the current bytes and describe the new version.

failureRecipes.message: This build selects no renderer.
failureRecipes.next: Describe and select stay available; only rendering is missing.

verify.description: Registers media, maps a selection to original coordinates, and refuses a region outside the declared bounds.

presentation.description: Teaches Claude Code to inspect original media metadata and validate coordinate regions.

skills.content:
Plot two declared numeric columns from one immutable table version.
Use capability.list to discover data.plot.

1. Bind the exact {id, version} of a registered table. The plot reports the resource it
   read, so a chart never drifts from the bytes behind it.
2. Both coordinates must be declared numeric columns. The table must have an entity key
   and namespace, because each point carries its key.
3. A point budget downsamples with a deterministic stride; the reply says so and reports
   originalPoints, so a sparse chart is never mistaken for sparse data.
4. Plotting reads only. It runs no code and changes no resource; if the file changed, the
   version is stale instead of silently mixing two states.
skills.intent: Plot two numeric columns of one table version, bounded and reproducible.

failureRecipes.message: Entity interaction requires an explicit unique key and namespace.
failureRecipes.next: Register the table with a key column and namespace before plotting it.

failureRecipes.message: Declare numeric scatter coordinate fields.
failureRecipes.next: Name two columns declared as number; a string column cannot be a coordinate.

failureRecipes.message: Resource version changed.
failureRecipes.next: Re-register the current bytes and plot the new version.

failureRecipes.message: Plot request exceeds the point budget.
failureRecipes.next: Lower maxPoints or accept the deterministic downsample the reply reports.

verify.description: A plot names the exact table version it read, downsamples to the point budget, and a changed file makes the version stale.

presentation.description: Teaches Claude Code to bind chart columns and keep point selections tied to stable rows.

skills.content:
Ask about a selected object and follow the answer without rebasing what was submitted.
Discover enabled operations with capability.list and skill.list.

1. An annotation anchors to an exact version: a UTF-16 document range or a stable table
   entity key at that resource version. A submitted message and its source snapshot stay
   exactly as submitted; a later edit does not silently move them.
2. annotation.create submits; annotation.read and annotation.list observe; annotation.reply
   answers and must name replyTo explicitly. Threads advance conditionally.
3. To hand chosen feedback to an agent, build it with context.create and read it back
   through the tool with context.read. Prepared, read and explicitly replied are three
   different facts: reading is not understanding and not completion.
4. Keep the original changeId after a lost acknowledgement and query the receipt boundary;
   never resubmit the same feedback under a new identity.

presentation.description: Teaches Claude Code to preserve versioned anchors and link replies to submitted comments.

skills.intent: Submit and follow anchored feedback without rebasing the original message.

failureRecipes.message: Anchor or thread advanced past the submitted version.
failureRecipes.next: Read the thread, then reply with an explicit replyTo instead of moving the original anchor.

failureRecipes.message: Selection or anchor is outside this binding.
failureRecipes.next: Anchor inside the document or table the binding owns.

failureRecipes.message: Anchor range or entity key is malformed.
failureRecipes.next: Use UTF-16 offsets for documents and a declared entity key for tables.

verify.description: Submits anchored messages over versioned drafts, advances threads conditionally and keeps original snapshots.

skills.content:
Prepare exact context and work through one registered native binding.
Use capability.list to discover context.create, context.read and the binding operations.

1. context.create freezes an exact source snapshot: a document range at one version or a
   table selection at one resource version. It prepares facts; it does not decide what
   they mean.
2. Fetch that context with context.read and use the tool result as your context. Reading
   is not understanding, and neither is task completion.
3. binding.open attaches one native session to one task and role. The attachment names
   the adapter registration and its transport capabilities; nothing else starts a
   native session.
4. Keep original identities. After a lost acknowledgement query the owner instead of
   opening a second binding under a new identity.
skills.intent: Give a native session exact prepared context and keep its binding identity.

failureRecipes.message: Context source version changed.
failureRecipes.next: Build a new context from the current version; do not edit through an old snapshot.

failureRecipes.message: Binding belongs to a different task or principal.
failureRecipes.next: Use the binding issued for this task and role; a forged attachment is refused.

failureRecipes.message: No native adapter is registered.
failureRecipes.next: Ask the operator to register the adapter for this project before opening a binding.

verify.description: Registers a native adapter, opens a business binding, refuses a forged one, and records artifact-ready observations without a model call.

presentation.description: Teaches Claude Code to fetch explicit context and preserve the original identity of changes.

skills.content:
Answer feedback that arrived through the selected native hook, without rebasing it.
Use capability.list to discover feedback.read and feedback.status.

1. When the hook supplies an original delivery reference, call feedback.read with that
   task, delivery, context and a stable fetchId. Fetch the whole object: if the reply says
   the size is too small, raise maxBytes rather than accepting a partial message.
2. feedback.status reports delivery, exact-target fetches and explicitly linked replies.
   A hook emission or a tool read is not understanding, model consumption or domain
   correctness.
3. relatedDocumentId is a pointer, not a snapshot: read that document CURRENT version
   before editing, preserve human changes, and use conditional edit and save.
4. Reply with annotation.reply, naming the exact original messageId as replyTo and a
   separate versioned reply draft.
5. Missing acknowledgements keep the outcome unknown. Do not invent a new delivery, a new
   native session, or a new changeId for the same reply.
skills.intent: Read one original feedback delivery and answer it explicitly.

failureRecipes.message: Feedback object exceeds maxBytes.
failureRecipes.next: Increase maxBytes and read the whole object; never use a partial message.

failureRecipes.message: Related document changed since the feedback.
failureRecipes.next: Read the current document version and edit conditionally, keeping human changes.

failureRecipes.message: Only the original business binding may read this delivery.
failureRecipes.next: Read it from the binding that received the delivery.

verify.description: Drives the real feedback worker and hook entries without a model: original delivery, whole-object fetch and explicit reply.

presentation.description: Reads original feedback, preserves current human edits and links an explicit reply.

skills.content:
Enhance only what the assigned person is looking at, within the presentation role.
Use rho_index, rho_resolve and rho_call for workspace.observe and workspace.enhance only.

1. Resolve the relevant instructions and whole exact contracts, including every schema
   dependency, before executing. Reuse only complete cached bodies; if context loses a
   body, omit its known reference and fetch it again.
2. Observe with workspace.observe, accumulating whole pages against the same snapshot.
   Use the assigned task, composition, presenter generation, retained binding witness and
   visible observation as the basis.
3. Enhance display only: emphasis, a title, and an optional plain note of at most 600
   characters. The application writes authorship and the basis; you do not.
4. Never read or write business feedback, shared documents or native trace through
   another capability.
5. Keep the original changeId after an unknown reply. A stale layout or assignment needs a
   fresh observation and an explicit new intent, never a silent rebase.
skills.intent: Enhance the visible layout for the assigned presenter, display only.

failureRecipes.message: Witness, generation or layout changed.
failureRecipes.next: Observe again and form an explicit new intent; never rebase silently.

failureRecipes.message: Presentation role cannot reach business feedback or documents.
failureRecipes.next: Stay within workspace.observe and workspace.enhance.

failureRecipes.message: Note exceeds 600 characters.
failureRecipes.next: Shorten the note; emphasis and title carry the rest.

verify.description: Presentation enhances display within its witness and role, and refuses business feedback or document access.

presentation.description: Enhances the assigned visible layout without business feedback or document access.
